newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ymos sees turn to oper profit in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Ymos sees turn to oper profit in 1998.

text.p: German autoparts group Ymos AG said on Tuesday it expected to improve its operating earnings significantly in 1997 and turn an operating profit in 1998.

The company, which reported a drop in net profits for 1996, also said its sales rose by 13 million marks to 207 million marks in the first four months of the year and pre-tax profits advanced by about 10 million marks in the period.
"Ymos will end the 1997 business year with clearly improved operating earnings. However we will only return to profitable territory in operating business in 1998," Ymos said.
Ymos said its earnings in 1996, when group net profit fell by 2.4 million marks to 16.4 million marks, were affected by both extraordinary income and costs.
The sale last year of its locking systems unit added 93.4 million marks to the group result, while earnings were reduced by high restructuring costs and spending on risk provisions.
Group sales rose marginally in 1996 to 957 million marks from 950 million marks.
Following the sale of its locking systems business, Ymos said it planned to achieve sales of 650 million marks in the current year, with the total boosted by new orders.
